transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. I feel like how I look and what I weigh is the only thing that matters about me now, and it’s starting to take over my life around food. It has just become so exhausting to have these thoughts constantly running through my head.
Do you restrict your food intake, binge eat, or use behaviors like vomiting or excessive exercise to control your weight?

Yes, I do. I try to restrict myself by skipping meals or only eating plain chicken and vegetables because I'm terrified of gaining weight, but then I'll lose control at night and eat massive amounts of food in secret. Afterward, I feel so guilty that I force myself to throw up in the bathroom just to undo the damage so I don't wake up heavier.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were ["F42", "F43.2", "F43.23", "F90.1", "F50.0", "F50.2"], but based on the patient's description of restrictive eating, recurrent episodes of binge eating, and compensatory behaviors such as self-induced vomiting driven by fear of weight gain, the presentation is highly consistent with an eating disorder characterized by these core features. The presence of bingeing and purging strongly supports F50.2 (bulimia nervosa), while other conditions like obsessive-compulsive disorder (F42), adjustment disorders (F43.2, F43.23), hyperkinetic disorder (F90.1), and anorexia nervosa (F50.0) are less consistent with the described pattern of eating behavior. Anorexia nervosa typically involves significant underweight and often lacks regular binge-purge episodes, whereas the patient’s cycle of restriction, loss of control, and purging aligns best with F50.2. Therefore, F50.2 is now the sole candidate.

No previous candidates were provided, so this is the initial differential based on presentation of obsessive thinking about appearance and weight impacting functioning.
